title: Major organs of the human body and what they do
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Knowing where your organs are and what each one does makes sense of how food, air and blood move through you. It is the first map every doctor, nurse and biology student learns.

How to hold it: Your own body is a ready-made memory palace. Walk it from top to bottom: brain, then the thyroid and esophagus in the neck, the heart and lungs in the chest, the five organs of the upper belly, the kidneys at the back, the intestines and bladder low down, and the skin wrapped around it all. Touch each spot as you name it and say its job in a few words. Chunking by region keeps each stop to five or fewer.
This list has 16 items. Answer below, then check — the practice button generates fresh questions from the list itself.
